correctness.rationale: For v in blade B_i the closed neighborhood is {c} union B_i, so signed dominance is exactly e+S_i>=1; for e=+1 this yields S_i>=0, and for e=-1 S_i>=2. Center inequality is automatic for r>=2. Independent binomial choices per blade give the two-term weight polynomial, with Q_1=0 as a correct boundary case; minima are 1+o in + branch and -1+2r+o in - branch, with latter strictly larger if feasible. Independently brute-forced original vertexwise neighborhood sums for 35 heterogeneous size tuples comprising 4856 sign labelings; all exact coefficient maps and minimum counts match.

value.rationale: An entire exact weight enumerator and full minimum-family description for arbitrary unequal clique sizes constitutes a natural, reusable signed-domination invariant of a graph family whose homogeneous special case was already studied. It answers more than minimum weight: counts all feasible signed labelings by weight, displays parity dependence and central-label rigidity, potentially usable for signed forcing/extremal questions. The proof is elementary but the complete heterogeneous all-weight invariant, not a renaming of the known homogeneous scalar, is the motivated result.
